effect_types.definition: Worker or collective actor receives evidence, factors, reasons, data, or logic sufficient to inspect the exertion.
An authorised actor can stop, suspend, or hold processing or adverse action before further harm.
Access, account, duties, status, or records are restored to an affected worker.
Backpay, damages, or other money is paid to an affected worker rather than to a regulator.
A feature, data use, monitoring practice, or system use is removed or prohibited.
A decision workflow, notice process, review rule, retention practice, or policy is changed.
Model features, thresholds, training data, score logic, or decision data are changed.
Implementation is checked later and results remain available to workers or collective actors.

interpretive_rule: A counterpower effect is classified by what changed: evidence access, immediate processing, an individual outcome, worker money, a feature or use, a workflow or policy, a model or data object, or later verification and collective memory.
